message.content:
**Order executed:** buy 44 AAPL @ limit $222.75 → filled at $222.75, total ≈ $9,801.00.

**Summary paragraph:** Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended September 28, 2024) results, released October 31, 2024, showed quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and for the full fiscal year 2024 total net sales of **$391.0 billion** ($391,035 million, versus $383,285 million in fiscal 2023), with net income of $93,736 million and diluted EPS of $6.08 — including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge that depressed net income slightly below the prior year's $96,995 million. I verified these figures against both Apple's newsroom release and Apple's Form 10-K filed with the SEC, and the two sources agree. That combination — record annual revenue with modest growth, healthy mid-20s operating margin ($123,216 million operating income), and a purely one-off drag on earnings — supported a constructive view on AAPL, so I placed a single buy order well within your mandate: 44 shares at a limit of $222.75, essentially at the current market (last $222.70, ask $222.72), for a notional of about $9,801 — under the $10,000 per-order cap, far under the $20,000 daily total, buy-side only, in a permitted ticker, with no cash withdrawn from the account (cash before the order was $50,000; existing position: 100 shares of MSFT, untouched). I chose one order rather than scaling in because the mandate's per-order and daily limits leave room for only two such orders and the setup did not warrant splitting the position.
